policies.name: CA001 - Block legacy authentication
policies.summary: Blocks Exchange ActiveSync and other legacy protocols (POP, IMAP, SMTP AUTH, older Office clients) for everyone.
policies.why: Legacy protocols cannot perform MFA, so attackers use them for password spray and credential stuffing. Microsoft reports that the vast majority of password spray attacks use legacy authentication.
policies.impact: Old mail clients, multifunction printers and scripts that use basic authentication will stop working. Check sign-in logs filtered by Client app before enforcing.

policies.name: CA002 - Require phishing-resistant MFA for administrators
policies.summary: Requires the built-in Phishing-resistant MFA authentication strength (FIDO2 security key, passkey, Windows Hello for Business or certificate) for 15 admin roles.
policies.why: Admin accounts are the top target. Push notifications and one-time codes can be phished through adversary-in-the-middle proxies; phishing-resistant methods are bound to the real sign-in site.
policies.impact: Admins without a FIDO2 key, passkey or Windows Hello for Business will be blocked. Issue methods first, and use a Temporary Access Pass to bootstrap registration.

policies.name: CA003 - Require MFA for all users
policies.summary: Requires multifactor authentication for every user and every cloud app.
policies.why: MFA blocks the large majority of account compromise attacks that rely on stolen or guessed passwords.
policies.impact: Users must register an MFA method. The Directory Synchronization Accounts role is excluded so Entra Connect keeps syncing; exclude other service accounts only if they cannot use workload identities.

policies.name: CA004 - Require MFA for Azure management
policies.summary: Requires MFA for the Azure portal, Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell and other tools that use Azure Resource Manager.
policies.why: Anyone with an Azure RBAC role can change infrastructure. This closes the gap for users who hold subscription roles but no Entra admin role.
policies.impact: Automation that signs in as a user to Azure Resource Manager will need to move to a managed identity or service principal.

policies.name: CA005 - Require MFA for guests and external users
policies.summary: Requires MFA for B2B guests and other external users.
policies.why: Guest accounts are protected by another organization's security. Requiring MFA in your tenant ensures a stolen guest password alone cannot reach your data.
policies.impact: Guests register MFA in your tenant on first access, unless you trust their home tenant's MFA through cross-tenant access settings.

policies.name: CA006 - Require compliant or hybrid-joined device (Windows and macOS)
policies.summary: Allows desktop access only from devices that are Intune compliant or Microsoft Entra hybrid joined.
policies.why: Stolen credentials and session tokens are far less useful when access also requires a managed, healthy device.
policies.impact: Personal computers lose access. Roll out device enrollment and compliance policies first, and keep this in report-only until the logs show near-full compliance.

policies.name: CA007 - Block unknown or unsupported device platforms
policies.summary: Blocks sign-ins from device platforms that are not Android, iOS, Windows, macOS or Linux.
policies.why: Attack tooling often sends unusual or spoofed platform strings. Blocking unknown platforms removes a common way around device-based policies.
policies.impact: Rarely affects real users. Check report-only results for legitimate unusual clients before enforcing.

policies.name: CA008 - Require MFA for medium and high sign-in risk
policies.summary: When Microsoft Entra ID Protection rates a sign-in as medium or high risk, the user must complete MFA every time.
policies.why: Catches sign-ins from anonymous IPs, impossible travel, password spray patterns and token anomalies, and challenges them in real time.
policies.impact: Needs Entra ID P2. Users must already be registered for MFA, or risky sign-ins will be blocked.

policies.name: CA009 - Require secure password change for high user risk
policies.summary: When a user's credentials are likely compromised (for example, found in a leak), they must complete MFA and change their password.
policies.why: Lets users remediate their own leaked credentials immediately instead of waiting for the help desk.
policies.impact: Needs Entra ID P2 and self-service password reset. For hybrid users, enable password writeback.

policies.name: CA010 - Secure security info registration
policies.summary: Requires MFA to register or change MFA methods from outside your trusted locations.
policies.why: If an attacker gets a password before the user registers MFA, they could register their own phone. This stops that.
policies.impact: New hires working remotely need a Temporary Access Pass to register their first method. Define trusted named locations before enforcing.

policies.name: CA011 - Admin session limits
policies.summary: Admins re-authenticate every 4 hours and browser sessions are never persistent.
policies.why: Limits how long a stolen admin session cookie stays useful and stops 'stay signed in' on shared machines.
policies.impact: Admins sign in more often. Pair with PIM so admin roles are only active when needed.

policies.name: CA012 - Require app protection on mobile devices
policies.summary: On iOS and Android, allows access only through apps with an Intune app protection policy, such as Outlook and Teams.
policies.why: Protects company data on personal phones (blocks copy/paste to personal apps, enables selective wipe) without enrolling the whole device.
policies.impact: Native mail apps and unsupported third-party apps lose access. Create Intune app protection policies first.
